purpose: Planning registry for the AI-BS core game engine. This is not a build manifest or an installation inventory.

version_policy.selection_point: Resolve the selected distribution at its introducing milestone before the first integration build.
version_policy.selected_versions: Null until compiled; verified integrations record an immutable pin and scoped evidence. Most entries remain proposed.
version_policy.update_rule: Update a dependency pin in an explicit change with its build options, notices, compatibility checks and relevant milestone validation.

scope_notes.required_for_v01: Required by the proposed engine and editor v0.1 milestone set; this does not mean every entry is shipped with the player.
scope_notes.ships_in: Proposed use or packaging scope. development_only means local development tooling, not automatic redistribution. A format entry describes supported data rather than a bundled implementation.
scope_notes.verification: integration_status describes the new native-engine integration. Existing source evidence does not establish an installed SDK, a compiled integration, runtime availability or license compatibility.
scope_notes.installation_status: Per-entry installation_status is verified only for explicitly tested integrations; this registry is not a full machine inventory.

entries.name: C++20
entries.role: Language baseline for engine runtime, module interfaces and build targets.
entries.license_summary: Language standard selection; the compiler and standard-library distribution have their own terms.
caveats: Require a full C++20 compiler; current EnTT upstream requires at least C++20.
Keep engine SDK boundaries independent of third-party C++ object layouts.

entries.name: MSVC C++ toolchain
entries.role: Windows x64 compiler, linker, debugger and C/C++ runtime selection.
entries.license_summary: Microsoft publisher terms; verify the selected distribution and redistributable components.
caveats: Record exact compiler/toolset and runtime linkage choices.
An installed compiler does not establish a successful engine configuration or build.

entries.name: Windows SDK
entries.role: Windows headers, import libraries and Direct3D/DXGI development interfaces.
entries.license_summary: Microsoft publisher terms; verify the selected SDK distribution and redistribution rights for chosen components.
caveats: Pin the SDK version with the toolchain.
The Windows SDK is distinct from the legacy DirectX SDK and optional DirectX Agility SDK.

entries.name: CMake
entries.role: Configure engine targets, dependency integration, build presets and test targets.
entries.license_summary: Kitware publisher license and notices; verify the selected distribution.
caveats: Pin a tested CMake release.
Use repository-local presets and separate generated build directories.

entries.name: Ninja
entries.role: Build executor for the proposed CMake workflow.
entries.license_summary: Upstream distribution terms and notices; verify the selected distribution.
caveats: Use the same generator and configuration conventions in developer and automated builds.
Record the executable version independently of the CMake version.

entries.name: vcpkg
entries.role: Dependency acquisition and reproducible package integration.
entries.license_summary: Microsoft/upstream publisher terms; individual ports retain their own licenses.
caveats: Pin the vcpkg baseline and explicit dependency versions or overrides.
A package-manager baseline does not establish that all selected packages build together.
This registry does not create a vcpkg manifest or download any port.

entries.name: SDL3
entries.role: Window lifecycle, display handling, keyboard, mouse and controller input.
entries.license_summary: zlib license, as documented by SDL.
caveats: Use SDL3 platform/input facilities with AI-BS-owned Direct3D 12 rendering.
Do not add a second renderer through SDL_Renderer without an explicit architecture decision.
Establish one event-loop owner when connecting the standalone runtime to the Qt editor.

entries.name: Direct3D 12 and DXGI
entries.role: Initial Windows renderer backend, presentation, GPU commands and resource state management.
entries.license_summary: Microsoft publisher/runtime terms; verify the selected SDK and redistributable components.
caveats: Application code owns command submission, resource-state transitions and synchronization.
Declare the supported feature baseline and query device capabilities.
Ray tracing and additional backends are later milestones.

entries.name: DirectX Shader Compiler
entries.role: Compile HLSL into versioned shader artifacts for the Direct3D 12 backend.
entries.license_summary: Upstream LLVM Release License and bundled third-party notices; verify the selected DXC distribution.
caveats: Pin compiler, shader-model target and flags in cooked artifact metadata.
Ship precompiled shaders in the player; runtime source compilation is not a v0.1 requirement.
Do not describe all bundled DXC code as a single MIT component.

entries.name: DirectXMath
entries.role: SIMD mathematics and graphics transforms behind AI-BS math types.
entries.license_summary: MIT license, as documented by Microsoft.
caveats: Specify coordinate handedness, matrix convention, units and quaternion serialization in engine contracts.
Do not expose SIMD-specific layouts in save files or the external SDK ABI.

entries.name: Dear ImGui
entries.role: Runtime diagnostics and early inspector/debug panels.
entries.license_summary: MIT license for Dear ImGui; the optional Dear ImGui Test Engine is a separate product.
caveats: Use maintained SDL3 or Win32 platform backend plus the Direct3D 12 renderer backend.
Pin a release/commit; docking and multiple-viewports features require a deliberate branch selection.
Keep Qt as the proposed outer editor shell and ImGui as runtime tooling to avoid competing editor architectures.

entries.name: EnTT
entries.role: Entity/component storage and optional reflection/event helpers behind engine-owned contracts.
entries.license_summary: MIT license for EnTT source; documentation has separately stated licenses.
caveats: Current upstream README requires C++20.
EnTT does not define AI-BS component attributes, persistent entity identities, editor undo or schema migration.
Serialize stable engine IDs and registered fields, not raw ECS handles.

entries.name: cgltf
entries.role: Import glTF/GLB source scenes into the AI-BS asset cooker.
entries.license_summary: MIT license.
caveats: Parsing does not automatically load or decode all external buffer/image content.
Compressed extensions require the corresponding decoder/transcoder.
Document the accepted glTF subset and reject unsupported required extensions.
Use cooked engine assets in the player rather than unrestricted source-scene parsing.

entries.name: glTF 2.0 and GLB
entries.role: Source interchange format for meshes, materials, scenes, skins and animation.
entries.license_summary: Khronos specification terms apply to the specification; importer and codec implementations have their own licenses.
caveats: A file format is not an SDK or a complete runtime asset pipeline.
Define supported extensions, coordinate conversion, tangents, material channels and texture color spaces.
Validate required extensions and resource references during import.

entries.name: DirectXTex
entries.role: Offline texture conversion, mip generation and Windows/DX12 texture cooking.
entries.license_summary: MIT license, as documented by Microsoft.
caveats: Upstream describes the full processing library as primarily intended for tools.
Current upstream requires Windows 11 SDK 22000 or later for Visual Studio builds.
Select a minimal runtime cooked-texture loader separately; do not ship the full cooker by default.

entries.name: D3D12 Memory Allocator
entries.role: GPU heap suballocation and resource allocation bookkeeping.
entries.license_summary: MIT license.
caveats: Allocation support does not replace engine fences, resource lifetime tracking, descriptors or resource barriers.
Query real device budgets and track the engine's own GPU allocations.
Pin compile-time options and integrate behind the renderer allocation interface.

entries.name: Jolt Physics
entries.role: Rigid bodies, collision queries, triggers and character-controller foundation.
entries.license_summary: MIT license.
caveats: Current README specifies VS2022+, Clang16+ or GCC12+ and uses C++17.
Use a bounded fixed-step update and explicit physics/world ownership.
Determinism has documented limits; do not claim cross-platform replay equivalence automatically.
Select CPU instruction baseline, precision and build options before recording reproducibility evidence.
entries.implemented_scope: Matching quaternion-oriented static boxes, grounded capsule with20/30degree supported slopes and60degree reject/sliding, fixed ticks, swept camera spheres; Debug/Release installed SDK and native motherboard obstacle course verified.
entries.remaining_scope: Moving/rotating bodies, dynamic rigid bodies, triggers, vehicles, fluids, terrain and broader planned physics roles remain unimplemented.
entries.milestone_reconciliation: Current BUILD_ROADMAP M1 supersedes historical M3 introduction label for this integration; other historical stage labels in this registry are not the active queue.

entries.name: miniaudio
entries.role: Device playback, mixing, spatial audio and Adam dialogue playback.
entries.license_summary: Choice of public-domain dedication or MIT No Attribution; proposed selection is MIT-0.
caveats: Current manual describes including miniaudio.h and compiling miniaudio.c, or linking a library; do not assume historical header-only packaging.
ABI compatibility is not guaranteed between versions, including bugfix releases.
Audio callbacks must avoid blocking inference, file I/O and engine locks.

entries.name: SQLite
entries.role: Versioned save-state storage behind the engine persistence service.
entries.license_summary: Core SQLite library is public domain; ancillary distribution scripts can have separate terms.
caveats: Existing Python sqlite3 use does not establish the native adapter or game-save schema.
Use bounded asynchronous writes and a declared single-writer policy.
Keep game state in namespaced tables and support portable standalone saves without requiring an AI-BS backend process.

existing_source_evidence.observation: Imports Python sqlite3; this is not a compiled native-engine integration.

entries.implemented_scope: Pinned static SQLite, scoped atomic components/events/receipts, bounded worker/world publication, native FirstBoot HUD/live retry/reload/close, offline outcome recall and validated non-destructive original-save import; verified source/installed SDK and Studio92 player.
entries.remaining_scope: Full-history startup replay/whole-world copies remain alpha limits. Future schema migrations, streamed recovery and broader campaign/creator systems remain later work.
entries.milestone_reconciliation: Current M2 supersedes the historical M3 introduction label; most other registry entries remain proposed.

entries.name: Existing PyQt6 editor shell
entries.role: Integrate engine project tools with the existing native AI-BS studio.
entries.license_summary: PyQt is GPLv3 or Riverbank Commercial License; PyQt itself is not LGPL. Qt has separate distribution terms.
caveats: Retain the existing editor shell while the runtime owns its event loop and renderer.
Standalone player excludes PyQt6, Python and editor-only components.
Verify selected distribution terms for editor packaging without asserting overall project license compatibility.

existing_source_evidence.observation: Imports PyQt6.QtCore for the existing desktop task bus; new engine/editor integration remains unverified.

entries.name: Lua
entries.role: Later mission/gameplay scripting through registered engine capabilities.
entries.license_summary: MIT license.
caveats: Defer until the component schema and validated gameplay command interface work.
Specify API exposure, execution budgets, error handling and reload semantics.
Embedded scripting does not automatically provide isolation or unrestricted engine-memory access policies.

entries.name: KTX2 texture workflow
entries.role: Later portable/supercompressed texture workflow when asset requirements justify it.
entries.license_summary: Khronos format/specification terms and separate licenses for the selected encoder/transcoder implementation.
caveats: KTX2 is a format, not a decoder implementation.
Select and pin the actual encoder/transcoder and preserve its bundled notices.
cgltf recognizing KHR_texture_basisu does not perform transcoding.
Keep the initial Windows texture cooker focused on the selected DX12 runtime format.

entries.name: DirectX Agility SDK
entries.role: Optional later Direct3D runtime deployment for features beyond the selected OS baseline.
entries.license_summary: Microsoft publisher terms; verify selected package and redistributable runtime components.
caveats: Not required for the initial renderer until a concrete feature needs it.
Record OS, driver and feature requirements with the selected package.
Do not add Agility deployment complexity solely to claim the newest SDK.

entries.name: PIX on Windows
entries.role: Development GPU/timing captures, memory analysis and DX12 diagnosis.
entries.license_summary: Microsoft publisher terms; verify selected PIX and optional WinPixEventRuntime distributions.
caveats: Development-only tool; installation or redistribution is not implied.
Optional instrumentation runtime has its own version and packaging decision.
Capture validation should use real engine execution and measured timings.

entries.name: RenderDoc
entries.role: Alternative development frame capture and graphics inspection.
entries.license_summary: MIT license for RenderDoc; preserve selected distribution notices if redistributing.
caveats: Official README documents D3D12, D3D11, Vulkan and OpenGL capture support.
Development-only tool, not a mandatory player dependency.
Validate the selected release against the engine's actual feature subset.

entries.name: Recast Navigation and Detour
entries.role: Researched candidate for tiled navigation generation, runtime queries and construction-aware regional updates.
entries.license_summary: Zlib license; verify selected distribution notices and build options.
caveats: Tiled mesh rebakes and temporary obstacle updates are distinct workflows.
New walkable surfaces such as constructed bridges require updated source geometry and rebaking or an appropriate explicit traversal link.
World edits need dirty bounds, tile generations, bounded queues and stale-result rejection; library selection alone does not implement these policies.
Pin and compile only when the navigation milestone requires it; no installation or player integration is claimed.
